restactions.filter:
def commas: tostring
  | if (length <= 3) then .
    else ((.[0:(length%3)]) as $h
          | ([$h] + [range(length%3; length; 3) as $i | .[$i:$i+3]])
          | map(select(. != "")) | join(","))
    end;
def num: if . == null then 0 else (tonumber? // 0) end;
((.usage.data) // []) as $rows
| { rows: [ $rows[]
    | (.input_tokens | num) as $in
    | (.cached_input_tokens | num) as $cached
    | {
        consumer: (if (.consumer // "") == "" then "unattributed" else .consumer end),
        team: (if (.team // "") == "" then "—" else .team end),
        model: (.model // "—"),
        provider: (.provider // "—"),
        calls: (.calls | num | commas),
        inputTokens: ($in | commas),
        cachedTokens: ($cached | commas),
        cachePct: (if (.cache_pct // null) == null then "—" else ((.cache_pct | tostring) + "%") end),
        outputTokens: (.output_tokens | num | commas),
        reasoningTokens: (.reasoning_tokens | num | commas),
        ttft: (if (.avg_ttft_s // null) == null then "—" else ((.avg_ttft_s | tostring) + "s") end),
        errors: (.errors | num | commas),
        rawInput: $in, rawOutput: (.output_tokens | num)
      } ],
    
    
    
    
    totals: {
      consumers: ($rows | length),
      inputTokens: ([ $rows[] | (.input_tokens | num) ] | add // 0 | commas),
      outputTokens: ([ $rows[] | (.output_tokens | num) ] | add // 0 | commas),
      calls: ([ $rows[] | (.calls | num) ] | add // 0 | commas)
    } }

restactions.name: agents-topology
restactions.filter:
# snowplow writes a swallowed step error to its errorKey as an ACCUMULATING SLICE, each entry
# being the apiserver Status decoded to a map or a bare message string. Flatten all three shapes;
# "" means the step SUCCEEDED. Same helper as restaction.agents-list.
def errText($e):
  if $e == null then ""
  else ( [ ( $e | if type == "array" then .[] else . end )
           | if type == "object" then ((.message // .reason // (. | tojson)))
             elif . == null then ""
             else tostring end ]
         | map(select(. != "")) | unique | join("; ") )
  end;

# [scheme://]<svc>[.<ns>[.svc[.cluster.local]]][:port][/path] -> "<svc>.<ns>". A bare single-label
# host takes the caller's own namespace, which is what in-cluster DNS would resolve it to.
def hostKey($h; $ns):
  ( ($h // "") | split("://") | (if length > 1 then .[1] else .[0] end)
    | split("/") | .[0] | split(":") | .[0] | split(".") ) as $p
  | if (($p | length) == 0) or (($p[0] // "") == "") then ""
    elif ($p | length) == 1 then ($p[0] + "." + $ns)
    else ($p[0] + "." + ($p[1] // $ns)) end;

def clip($s; $n):
  ( $s // "" ) | if (. | length) > $n then (.[0:$n] + "…") else . end;

( errText(.agentsError) )   as $agErr
| ( errText(.gatewaysError) ) as $gwErr
| ( errText(.routesError) )   as $rtErr
| ( errText(.backendsError) ) as $beErr
| ( errText(.serversError) )  as $srvErr
| ( [ (if $agErr  != "" then ("Agents (" + $agErr + ")") else empty end),
      (if $gwErr  != "" then ("Gateways (" + $gwErr + ")") else empty end),
      (if $rtErr  != "" then ("HTTPRoutes (" + $rtErr + ")") else empty end),
      (if $beErr  != "" then ("AgentgatewayBackends (" + $beErr + ")") else empty end),
      (if $srvErr != "" then ("RemoteMCPServers (" + $srvErr + ")") else empty end) ] ) as $failed

# One flat record per route. parentRef.kind and backendRef.kind both DEFAULT in the Gateway API
# (Gateway and Service respectively) — reading them as required would drop every route that
# omits them, which is most of them.
| ( [ (.routes.items // [])[]
      | . as $r
      | ($r.metadata.namespace // "") as $rns
      | { name: ($r.metadata.name // ""),
          ns:   $rns,
          hosts: [ ($r.spec.rules // [])[] | (.matches // [])[] | (.headers // [])[]
                   | select((((.name // "") | ascii_downcase) == "x-kagent-host"))
                   | (.value // "") | select(. != "") ],
          gws:  [ ($r.spec.parentRefs // [])[] | select(((.kind // "Gateway") == "Gateway"))
                  | ((.namespace // $rns) + "/" + (.name // "")) ],
          beRefs: [ ($r.spec.rules // [])[] | (.backendRefs // [])[]
                    | select(((.kind // "Service") == "AgentgatewayBackend"))
                    | ((.namespace // $rns) + "/" + (.name // "")) ],
          svcRefs: [ ($r.spec.rules // [])[] | (.backendRefs // [])[]
                     | select(((.kind // "Service") == "Service"))
                     | ((.name // "") + ":" + ((.port // 0) | tostring)) ],
          paths: [ ($r.spec.rules // [])[] | (.matches // [])[] | (.path.value // empty) ] } ] ) as $routes

| ( reduce ((.gateways.items // [])[]) as $g ({};
      .[(($g.metadata.namespace // "") + "/" + ($g.metadata.name // ""))] = $g) ) as $gwIdx
| ( reduce ((.backends.items // [])[]) as $b ({};
      .[(($b.metadata.namespace // "") + "/" + ($b.metadata.name // ""))] = $b) ) as $beIdx

# A hub is a Gateway some route attaches to AND routes on x-kagent-host. $hubsUnread are the ones
# whose routes we saw but whose object we could not read — counted, never drawn (no real uid).
| ( [ $routes[] | select((.hosts | length) > 0) | .gws[] ] | unique ) as $hubKeys
| ( [ $hubKeys[] | select($gwIdx[.] != null) ] ) as $hubs
| ( [ $hubKeys[] | select($gwIdx[.] == null) ] ) as $hubsUnread

# Per hub: every x-kagent-host it serves, carrying the route name that serves it so a green node
# can name its own evidence instead of just asserting "routed".
| ( reduce $hubs[] as $k ({};
      .[$k] = [ $routes[] | select((.gws | index($k)) != null) | . as $rr
                | (.hosts[] | hostKey(.; $rr.ns)) as $hk
                | { h: $hk, r: $rr.name } ] ) ) as $meshOf

# THE HONESTY GATE. Reachability is only asserted when the route list answered in full AND every
# hub listener takes routes from its own namespace only — otherwise a route could be sitting
# behind the caller's per-namespace refilter and "no route" would be a guess. "Same" is the
# Gateway API default, so an absent allowedRoutes block is the strict case, not the loose one.
| ( ( $rtErr == "" )
    and ( [ $hubs[] | $gwIdx[.] | (.spec.listeners // [])[]
            | (.allowedRoutes.namespaces.from // "Same") ] | all(. == "Same") ) ) as $routesComplete
| ( if $rtErr != "" then ("the HTTPRoute list did not answer (" + $rtErr + ")")
    else "this gateway accepts routes from namespaces beyond its own, which this page did not read" end ) as $whyUnsure
| ( [ $hubs[] | ($gwIdx[.].metadata.name // "") ] | join(", ") ) as $hubName

# Same bench predicate as restaction.agents-list: a composition-less Agent is a bench agent.
# Rows without a name or namespace are dropped — they cannot be keyed to a route host.
| ( [ (.agents.items // [])[]
      | select(((.metadata.name // "") != "") and ((.metadata.namespace // "") != "")) ] ) as $allAgents
| ( [ $allAgents[] | select((((.metadata.labels // {})["krateo.io/composition-id"]) != null) ) ] ) as $platformAgents
| ( [ $allAgents[] | select((((.metadata.labels // {})["krateo.io/composition-id"]) == null) ) ] ) as $benchAgents

# An agent attaches to the hub that carries its host. When no hub does and there is exactly one
# hub, it still attaches there — an unrouted agent belongs IN the picture (that is the finding),
# drawn with the orange marker. With several hubs and no match there is no honest edge to draw.
| ( [ $platformAgents[]
      | . as $a
      | (($a.metadata.name) + "." + ($a.metadata.namespace)) as $h
      | ( [ $hubs[] | select((([ $meshOf[.][] | select(.h == $h) ]) | length) > 0) ] ) as $onHubs
      | ( if ($onHubs | length) > 0 then $onHubs
          elif ($hubs | length) == 1 then $hubs else [] end ) as $attach
      | ( [ $hubs[] | $meshOf[.][] | select(.h == $h) | .r ] | unique ) as $viaRoutes
      | ( [ (($a.spec.declarative // {}).tools // [])[] | select(.type == "Agent") ] | length ) as $delegates
      | { hubs: $attach,
          n: { date: ($a.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
               kind: "Agent",
               name: ($a.metadata.name),
               namespace: ($a.metadata.namespace),
               resourceVersion: ($a.metadata.resourceVersion // ""),
               uid: ($a.metadata.uid // ""),
               version: ($a.apiVersion // "kagent.dev/v1alpha2"),
               icon: { name: (if $delegates > 0 then "fa-sitemap" else "fa-robot" end),
                       color: (if $delegates > 0 then "violet" else "blue" end),
                       message: ( clip(($a.spec.description // "no description"); 160)
                                  + (if $delegates > 0 then (" · delegates to " + ($delegates | tostring) + " agents over A2A") else "" end) ) },
               statusIcon: ( if ($routesComplete | not) then
                               { name: "fa-circle-question", color: "gray",
                                 message: ("Cannot tell whether anything can reach this agent: " + $whyUnsure + ". It is NOT being reported as unrouted.") }
                             elif ($viaRoutes | length) > 0 then
                               { name: "fa-check", color: "green",
                                 message: ("Reachable through " + $hubName + " — HTTPRoute " + ($viaRoutes | join(", ")) + " matches x-kagent-host: " + $h) }
                             else
                               { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                 message: ("No route on " + $hubName + " matches x-kagent-host: " + $h + " — nothing can delegate to this agent.") }
                             end ),
               parentRefs: [] } } ] | sort_by(.n.name) ) as $agentEntries

# The collapsed bench node. Its status is the WORST of its members', and names the ones that are
# missing a route — collapsing may cost a node, it must not cost the finding.
| ( [ $benchAgents[] | (.metadata.name + "." + .metadata.namespace) ] ) as $benchHosts
| ( if ($benchAgents | length) == 0 then []
    else
      [ ( [ $hubs[] | . as $k | select((([ $meshOf[$k][] | .h as $hh | select(($benchHosts | index($hh)) != null) ]) | length) > 0) ] ) as $onHubs
        | ( if ($onHubs | length) > 0 then $onHubs
            elif ($hubs | length) == 1 then $hubs else [] end ) as $attach
        | ( [ $benchAgents[] | .metadata.namespace ] | unique ) as $nss
        | { hubs: $attach,
            n: { date: ( [ $benchAgents[] | .metadata.creationTimestamp // "" ] | map(select(. != "")) | sort | (.[0] // "") ),
                 kind: "Agent · collapsed group",
                 name: ("bench profile (" + ($benchAgents | length | tostring) + " agents)"),
                 namespace: (if ($nss | length) == 1 then $nss[0] else "" end),
                 resourceVersion: "",
                 uid: "group:bench-agents",
                 version: ( [ $benchAgents[] | .apiVersion // "kagent.dev/v1alpha2" ] | unique | join(", ") ),
                 icon: { name: "fa-flask", color: "gray",
                         message: ("Collapsed: " + ([ $benchAgents[] | .metadata.name ] | sort | join(", "))
                                   + ". The bench profile duplicates the platform topology against the same gateway; it is drawn as one node so the platform fan stays legible. Date shown is the oldest member's.") },
                 statusIcon: ( if ($routesComplete | not) then
                                 { name: "fa-circle-question", color: "gray",
                                   message: ("Cannot tell how many are reachable: " + $whyUnsure + ".") }
                               else
                                 ( ( [ $benchAgents[] | (.metadata.name + "." + .metadata.namespace)
                                       | . as $bh | select((([ $hubs[] | $meshOf[.][] | select(.h == $bh) ]) | length) == 0) ] ) as $miss
                                   | if ($miss | length) == 0 then
                                       { name: "fa-check", color: "green",
                                         message: ("All " + ($benchAgents | length | tostring) + " reachable through " + $hubName + " by x-kagent-host.") }
                                     else
                                       { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                         message: (($miss | length | tostring) + " with no route on " + $hubName + ": " + ($miss | join(", "))) }
                                     end )
                               end ),
                 parentRefs: [] } } ]
    end ) as $benchEntries

| ( $agentEntries + $benchEntries ) as $sourceEntries

# Tool servers join to the hub by the host they DIAL, not by name: RemoteMCPServer
# `kagent-tool-server` dials kagent-tools.krateo-system, which is exactly the x-kagent-host the
# MCP route matches. $srvOffHub is the honest residue — a server this gateway has no route for
# (today: flux-schema-mcp-server, whose URL leaves the cluster). It is NOT drawn detached, which
# would assert its traffic bypasses the gateway; nothing here can prove that. It is named in the
# subtitle as what it actually is: a server with no route on this hub.
| ( [ (.servers.items // [])[]
      | . as $s
      | hostKey(($s.spec.url // ""); ($s.metadata.namespace // "")) as $h
      | { s: $s, h: $h,
          tools: ( ($s.status.discoveredTools // []) | length ),
          hubs: [ $hubs[] | select((([ $meshOf[.][] | select(.h == $h) ]) | length) > 0) ] } ] ) as $srvAll
| ( [ $srvAll[] | select((.hubs | length) > 0) ] ) as $srvRouted
| ( [ $srvAll[] | select((.hubs | length) == 0) ] ) as $srvOffHub
| ( ( $srvRouted | sort_by([ (- .tools), .s.metadata.name ]) | .[0] ) ) as $srvTop

| ( if $srvTop == null then []
    else [ { hubs: ($srvTop.hubs),
             n: { date: ($srvTop.s.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
                  kind: "RemoteMCPServer",
                  name: ($srvTop.s.metadata.name),
                  namespace: ($srvTop.s.metadata.namespace),
                  resourceVersion: ($srvTop.s.metadata.resourceVersion // ""),
                  uid: ($srvTop.s.metadata.uid // ""),
                  version: ($srvTop.s.apiVersion // "kagent.dev/v1alpha2"),
                  icon: { name: "fa-screwdriver-wrench", color: "orange",
                          message: (($srvTop.tools | tostring) + " tools discovered · " + ($srvTop.s.spec.url // "no url")
                                    + " · reached through " + $hubName + " on x-kagent-host: " + $srvTop.h) },
                  statusIcon: ( ( [ ($srvTop.s.status.conditions // [])[]
                                    | select(((.type == "Accepted") and (.status == "True")) | not) ] ) as $exc
                                | if ($exc | length) == 0 then
                                    { name: "fa-check", color: "green", message: "Accepted by kagent." }
                                  else
                                    { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                      message: ( [ $exc[] | ((.type // "?") + "=" + (.status // "?") + " " + (.message // "")) ] | join(" · ") ) }
                                  end ),
                  parentRefs: [] } } ]
    end ) as $topToolEntries

| ( [ $srvRouted[] | select(($srvTop == null) or (.s.metadata.uid != $srvTop.s.metadata.uid)) ] ) as $srvRest
| ( if ($srvRest | length) == 0 then []
    else [ { hubs: ( [ $srvRest[] | .hubs[] ] | unique ),
             n: { date: ( [ $srvRest[] | .s.metadata.creationTimestamp // "" ] | map(select(. != "")) | sort | (.[0] // "") ),
                  kind: "RemoteMCPServer · collapsed group",
                  name: ("MCP tool servers (" + ($srvRest | length | tostring) + ")"),
                  namespace: ( ( [ $srvRest[] | .s.metadata.namespace ] | unique ) as $nss
                               | if ($nss | length) == 1 then $nss[0] else "" end ),
                  resourceVersion: "",
                  uid: "group:mcp-tool-servers",
                  version: ( [ $srvRest[] | .s.apiVersion // "kagent.dev/v1alpha2" ] | unique | join(", ") ),
                  icon: { name: "fa-screwdriver-wrench", color: "gray",
                          message: ("Collapsed: " + ( [ $srvRest[] | (.s.metadata.name + " (" + (.tools | tostring) + ")") ] | sort | join(", "))
                                    + ". Every one is routed by " + $hubName + " on its own x-kagent-host. Date shown is the oldest member's.") },
                  statusIcon: ( ( [ $srvRest[] | select((([ (.s.status.conditions // [])[] | select(((.type == "Accepted") and (.status == "True")) | not) ]) | length) > 0) | .s.metadata.name ] ) as $bad
                                | if ($bad | length) == 0 then
                                    { name: "fa-check", color: "green",
                                      message: (( [ $srvRest[] | .tools ] | add | tostring) + " tools discovered across " + ($srvRest | length | tostring) + " servers; all Accepted.") }
                                  else
                                    { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                      message: ("Not Accepted: " + ($bad | join(", "))) }
                                  end ),
                  parentRefs: [] } } ]
    end ) as $restToolEntries

# The model upstream. Classified by SHAPE, not by name: an AgentgatewayBackend the hub routes to
# that carries a spec.ai block is the LLM hop. Matching on the name "…-llm" would miss a rename
# and would file the tts backend (spec.static) under the model.
| ( [ $hubs[] | . as $k | $routes[] | select((.gws | index($k)) != null) | .beRefs[] | { k: $k, b: . } ] ) as $hubBackendPairs
| ( [ $hubBackendPairs[] | select(((($beIdx[.b] // {}).spec // {}).ai) != null) | .b ] | unique ) as $aiBackendKeys
| ( [ $aiBackendKeys[]
      | . as $bk | $beIdx[$bk] as $b
      | ( (($b.spec.ai // {}).provider // {}) | to_entries | (.[0] // null) ) as $prov
      | { hubs: ( [ $hubBackendPairs[] | select(.b == $bk) | .k ] | unique ),
          n: { date: ($b.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
               kind: "AgentgatewayBackend",
               name: ($b.metadata.name),
               namespace: ($b.metadata.namespace),
               resourceVersion: ($b.metadata.resourceVersion // ""),
               uid: ($b.metadata.uid // ""),
               version: ($b.apiVersion // "agentgateway.dev/v1alpha1"),
               # The provider key is read generically (vertexai / openai / anthropic / …) and only
               # fields that are actually present are appended, so a provider shape we have never
               # seen still names itself instead of rendering an empty tooltip.
               icon: { name: "fa-brain", color: "violet",
                       message: ( ( if $prov == null then "model provider not stated in spec.ai.provider"
                                    else ( $prov.key
                                           + ( ($prov.value.projectId // "") | if . == "" then "" else (" · project " + .) end )
                                           + ( ($prov.value.region // "")    | if . == "" then "" else (" · region " + .) end )
                                           + ( ($prov.value.model // "")     | if . == "" then "" else (" · " + .) end ) )
                                    end )
                                  + " · reached over "
                                  + ( [ $routes[] | select(((.beRefs | index($bk)) != null)) | .paths[] | select(. != "") ] | unique | join(", ") ) ) },
               statusIcon: ( ( [ ($b.status.conditions // [])[]
                                 | select(((.type == "Accepted") and (.status == "True")) | not) ] ) as $exc
                             | if ($exc | length) == 0 then
                                 { name: "fa-check", color: "green", message: "Backend accepted by the gateway." }
                               else
                                 { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                   message: ( [ $exc[] | ((.type // "?") + "=" + (.status // "?") + " " + (.message // "")) ] | join(" · ") ) }
                               end ),
               parentRefs: [] } } ] | sort_by(.n.name) ) as $llmEntries

# The hub itself. Its tooltip is where the route census lives — including the a2a catch-all's
# Service target, which is stated here as the route fact it is rather than drawn as a node this
# action never read (see the header).
| ( [ $hubs[]
      | . as $k | $gwIdx[$k] as $g
      | ( [ $routes[] | select((.gws | index($k)) != null) ] ) as $rs
      | ( [ $rs[] | select((.hosts | length) > 0) ] | length ) as $hostRoutes
      | ( [ $rs[] | select((.hosts | length) == 0) | .svcRefs[] ] | unique ) as $catchAll
      | { hubs: [],
          n: { date: ($g.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
               kind: "Gateway",
               name: ($g.metadata.name),
               namespace: ($g.metadata.namespace),
               resourceVersion: ($g.metadata.resourceVersion // ""),
               uid: ($g.metadata.uid // ""),
               version: ($g.apiVersion // "gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1"),
               icon: { name: "fa-shield-halved", color: "darkBlue",
                       message: ( ($rs | length | tostring) + " routes attached · " + ($hostRoutes | tostring)
                                  + " selected by an x-kagent-host header · listeners "
                                  + ( [ ($g.spec.listeners // [])[] | ((.protocol // "?") + ":" + ((.port // 0) | tostring)) ] | join(", ") )
                                  + ( ( [ ($g.status.addresses // [])[] | .value // empty ] | join(", ") )
                                      | if . == "" then "" else (" · " + .) end )
                                  + ( ($catchAll | join(", ")) | if . == "" then "" else (" · catch-all → " + .) end ) ) },
               # Gateway carries many condition types; only Accepted/Programmed are read, because
               # those are the two this node is claiming. An unknown future condition type is not
               # silently folded into a green check, nor alarmed on.
               statusIcon: ( ( [ ($g.status.conditions // [])[]
                                 | select((((.type == "Accepted") or (.type == "Programmed")) and (.status == "True")) | not)
                                 | select((.type == "Accepted") or (.type == "Programmed")) ] ) as $exc
                             | if ($exc | length) == 0 then
                                 { name: "fa-check", color: "green", message: "Accepted and Programmed." }
                               else
                                 { name: "fa-triangle-exclamation", color: "orange",
                                   message: ( [ $exc[] | ((.type // "?") + "=" + (.status // "?")) ] | join(" · ") ) }
                               end ),
               parentRefs: [ ( $sourceEntries[] | select((.hubs | index($k)) != null) | { uid: .n.uid } ) ] } } ] ) as $hubEntries

# EDGE DIRECTION: the frontend builds one edge per parentRefs entry, source = ref.uid, target =
# the node (FlowChart/utils.ts toGraphData). So the fan-in lives on the HUB's parentRefs (every
# agent -> hub) and the fan-out on each sink's (hub -> backend). parentRefs entries carry `uid`
# AND NOTHING ELSE: uid is the only field toGraphData reads, and repeating kind/name/date there
# would create a second, silently divergent copy of a node's identity in the same document.
| ( ( $topToolEntries + $restToolEntries + $llmEntries )
    | map( .n.parentRefs = [ ( .hubs[] | . as $k | ($gwIdx[$k].metadata.uid // "") | select(. != "") | { uid: . } ) ] ) ) as $sinkEntries

# No hub, no picture. A bare column of agent cards with nothing to converge on asserts nothing and
# reads as a broken widget; the empty state plus the subtitle below says why instead.
| ( if ($hubs | length) == 0 then []
    else ( [ $sourceEntries[].n ] + [ $hubEntries[].n ] + [ $sinkEntries[].n ] ) end ) as $nodes

| { nodes: $nodes,
    # Nothing renders hubCount today; it is the one number that tells an empty graph apart from
    # a graph that resolved and found no hub, which is the first question asked when the canvas
    # comes back blank.
    hubCount: ($hubs | length),
    # Rendered verbatim by paragraph.agents-topology-subtitle. Every exception the graph cannot
    # draw — an unrouted agent, an unreadable route list, a tool server this hub does not front —
    # is named here in prose, because a node that is absent explains nothing on its own.
    subtitle: (
      if ($failed | length) > 0 and ($hubs | length) == 0 then
        ( "This diagram cannot be drawn — " + ($failed | join("; "))
          + ". Nothing is shown rather than a partial graph that would read as the whole topology." )
      elif ($hubs | length) == 0 then
        ( "No agent gateway is visible from here: no HTTPRoute you can read selects a backend by an x-kagent-host header, "
          + "so there is no hub to draw. That is not a claim that the cluster has none." )
      else
        ( "One gateway carries a route for every agent and every tool server the agents dial. "
          + $hubName + " has "
          + ( [ $hubs[] | . as $k | [ $routes[] | select((.gws | index($k)) != null) ] | length ] | add | tostring )
          + " routes attached, "
          + ( [ $hubs[] | . as $k | [ $routes[] | select((.gws | index($k)) != null) | select((.hosts | length) > 0) ] | length ] | add | tostring )
          + " of them selected by an x-kagent-host header naming the in-cluster host the CALLING agent dialled — that header is set by the caller, which is what makes this one gateway the place every hop passes through. "
          + "Read live from Agent, Gateway, HTTPRoute, AgentgatewayBackend and RemoteMCPServer objects."
          # WHICH NODES ARE GROUPS HAS TO BE SAID IN WORDS. The graph draws 12 sources for 15
          # agents; a reader who is not told that counts the picture and gets the topology wrong.
          # The `kind` on each group node says it too, but only to someone who opens the node.
          + ( ( [ (if ($benchEntries | length) > 0 then (($benchAgents | length | tostring) + " bench agents") else empty end),
                  (if ($restToolEntries | length) > 0 then (($srvRest | length | tostring) + " smaller tool servers") else empty end) ] )
              | if (. | length) == 0 then "" else (" Collapsed to one node each: " + (. | join(", and ")) + " — drag to pan, scroll to zoom.") end )
          + ( ( [ $agentEntries[] | select(.n.statusIcon.color == "orange") | .n.name ] )
              | if (. | length) == 0 then "" else (" " + (. | length | tostring) + " agent(s) have no route on this gateway: " + (. | join(", ")) + ".") end )
          + ( if ($routesComplete | not) then (" Reachability is shown as unknown on every node because " + $whyUnsure + ".") else "" end )
          + ( ( [ $srvOffHub[] | .s.metadata.name ] )
              | if (. | length) == 0 then "" else (" Not drawn: " + (. | length | tostring) + " tool server(s) with no route on this gateway (" + (. | join(", ")) + ") — their endpoint is not one this gateway fronts.") end )
          + ( if ($failed | length) > 0 then (" Some reads FAILED — " + ($failed | join("; ")) + " — so the graph is incomplete.") else "" end )
          + ( if ($hubsUnread | length) > 0 then (" " + ($hubsUnread | length | tostring) + " further gateway(s) carry agent routes but their Gateway object was not readable, so they are not drawn.") else "" end ) )
      end ),
    # Paragraph.type is a hard CRD enum (secondary|success|warning|danger) — never "". Exception-
    # only: `secondary` is the healthy default, `danger` for a failed read, an unrouted agent, or
    # a reachability answer this page had to withhold.
    subtitleType: ( if (($failed | length) > 0) or (($hubs | length) == 0)
                      or (($agentEntries | map(select(.n.statusIcon.color == "orange")) | length) > 0)
                      or (($routesComplete | not) and (($hubs | length) > 0))
                    then "danger" else "secondary" end ) }

restactions.name: alert-detail
restactions.filter:
("" | rtrimstr("/")) as $console | (.name // "") as $n | (.namespace // "default") as $ns | (.alert.spec // {}) as $sp | (.alert.status // {}) as $st | ($sp.displayName // .alert.metadata.name // $n) as $dn | ($st.state // "PENDING") as $state
  # krateo.io/paused: "true" — the alert-provider skips this alert's firings.
| (((.alert.metadata.annotations // {})["krateo.io/paused"] // "") == "true") as $paused | ($st.hyperdxAlertId // "") as $haid | ($st.hyperdxDashboardId // "") as $hdid
  # This alert's incidents, newest first: the ones carrying its label.
| ([ ((.incidents.items) // [])[]
     | select(((.metadata.labels // {})["observability.krateo.io/alert"] // .spec.alertRef.name // "") == $n) ]) as $incs
| ([ $incs[]
     | { name: (.metadata.name // ""), namespace: (.metadata.namespace // $ns),
         title: (if (.status.rootCause.statement // "") != "" then .status.rootCause.statement else ("Incident " + (.metadata.name // "")) end),
         state: (.status.state // "Analyzing"),
         error: (.status.error // ""),
         reportText: ((.status.report // "") | if type == "string" then . else "" end),
         structured: ((.status.rootCause.statement // "") != ""),
         when: (.spec.triggeredAt // .metadata.creationTimestamp // "") } ]
   | sort_by(.when) | reverse
   | map(. + { open: (.state != "Resolved" and .state != "Closed"),
               route: ("/incidents/" + .namespace + "/" + .name) })) as $shaped
| ($shaped[0] // null) as $rep | [ $shaped[] | select(.open) ] as $open | [ $shaped[] | select(.open | not) ] as $ended | (if ($shaped | length) > 1 then "latest analysis" else "analysis" end) as $an
  # Did the analysis produce a result, fail (status.error, or a provider error in the report), or produce nothing?
  | (if $rep == null then "" else ($rep.reportText // "") end) as $repText
  | ($rep != null and ((($rep.error // "") != "") or ($repText | test("Bad Request|Too Many Requests|STREAM_ERROR|token count|exceeds the maximum")))) as $repFailed
  | (if $rep == null then false elif $repFailed then false else (($rep.structured // false) or (($repText | length) > 0)) end) as $repProduced
| {
    displayName: $dn,
    where: ($sp.where // "all logs"),
    # "above 1" — thresholdType + threshold, empty-safe (never a bare " " or leading space).
    thresholdText: ((($sp.thresholdType // "") + " " + (($sp.threshold // 0) | tostring)) | ltrimstr(" ")),
    interval: ($sp.interval // ""),
    message: ($sp.message // ""),
    state: $state,
    phase: ($st.phase // "Pending"),
    paused: $paused,
    # State tag — same map as the /alerts table, but OK→green (palette: green=health only,
    # and a quiet-OK alert IS the healthy default), ALERT→red (failure), PENDING→orange
    # (transitional). "OK" kept verbatim — the literal HyperDX state word.
    stateLabel: ($state | if . == "ALERT" then "Alert" elif . == "PENDING" then "Pending" else . end),
    stateColor: ($state | if . == "ALERT" then "red" elif . == "PENDING" then "orange" elif . == "OK" then "green" else "gray" end),
    hyperdxAlertId: $haid,
    hyperdxDashboardId: $hdid,
    # HyperDX console deep-links — absent unless BOTH the deployer configured a console URL
    # AND the reconciler recorded the id (no default URL invented; nothing-hardcoded).
    alertLink: (if ($console != "" and $haid != "") then ($console + "/alerts/" + $haid) else "" end),
    dashboardLink: (if ($console != "" and $hdid != "") then ($console + "/dashboards/" + $hdid) else "" end),
    hasConsole: (($console != "") and (($haid != "") or ($hdid != ""))),
    # Autopilot seed for the detail-page "Investigate with Autopilot" button (the ask flow
    # the OLD /alerts row-click used, preserved here now the row deep-links to this page).
    # The button navigates to a LITERAL server-built /incidents?ask= href (the seed @uri-
    # encoded once, here — same pattern as composition-detail's diagnoseHref; a Button
    # navigate path is used verbatim, NOT re-encoded like a Table cell, so it must be
    # pre-encoded exactly once). The raw `ask` is also emitted for any raw consumer.
    ask: ("Investigate the \"" + $dn + "\" observability alert — it is currently " + $state + "; explain what it watches, why it is in this state, and give me the concrete next steps."),
    askHref: ("/incidents?ask=" + (("Investigate the \"" + $dn + "\" observability alert — it is currently " + $state + "; explain what it watches, why it is in this state, and give me the concrete next steps.") | @uri)),
    # ── THE PIPELINE WALK ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # An alert is not one object, it is a CHAIN: the CR, the HyperDX rule it syncs to, the
    # evaluation, the alert-provider pass that reads it as a firing, the investigation that
    # firing opens, and the incident that investigation becomes. Every hop can stop without the one before it noticing, and this
    # page said nothing about any of them — it showed a green "OK" for days while the
    # alert -> RCA loop was dead on a tool schema the model kept refusing.
    #
    # A numbered walk, not a graph: the chain is LINEAR, so nodes and edges buy nothing.
    # Same treatment as the agents seven-hop, for the same reason.
    #
    # Each step says what it READ, and the first hop that cannot proceed says so and stops
    # claiming anything about the hops after it.
    pipelineMd: ([
        ("1. **The alert exists.** Counts " + (if ($sp.where // "") == "" then "**all log rows**" else ("rows matching `" + ($sp.where) + "`") end)
         + ", firing when the count is " + (($sp.thresholdType // "above") + " " + (($sp.threshold // 0) | tostring))
         + " over " + (if ($sp.interval // "") == "" then "its evaluation window" else ("`" + $sp.interval + "`") end) + "."
         + (if ($sp.where // "") == "" then "\n    - An empty filter matches every log line on the cluster, so this fires on volume alone." else "" end)),
        (if $haid != "" then ("2. **Synced to HyperDX.** Rule `" + $haid + "`.")
         else "2. **NOT synced to HyperDX.** `status.hyperdxAlertId` is empty, so no rule evaluates this alert and nothing below can happen. The chain stops here." end),
        (if $haid == "" then empty
         elif $state == "ALERT" then "3. **Evaluated, and currently firing.** HyperDX reports state `ALERT`."
         elif $state == "OK" then "3. **Evaluated, currently quiet.** HyperDX reports state `OK` — the threshold is not being crossed."
         else ("3. **Evaluated, state `" + $state + "`.** Not yet a verdict.") end)
         + (if $haid != "" and $paused then "\n    - **Paused.** The alert-provider skips its firings: no incident opens. Open incidents keep their checks." else "" end),
        (if $haid == "" then empty
         elif ($shaped | length) > 1 then ("4. **Incidents were opened.** " + ($shaped | length | tostring) + " for this alert; the latest is `" + ($rep.name // "") + "`.")
         elif $rep != null then ("4. **An incident was opened.** `" + ($rep.name // "") + "`.")
         elif $state == "ALERT" and $paused then "4. No incident — this alert is paused, so its firings open none."
         elif $state == "ALERT" then "4. **No incident exists, and this alert is firing.** The alert-provider's next pass (every 60 s) should open one; no Incident carries this alert's label. Either no pass has run since the alert fired, or the alert-provider could not create one; its logs say which."
         else "4. No incident — this alert has not fired, so none is expected." end),
        (if $rep == null then empty
         elif $repProduced then ("5. **The " + $an + " produced a root cause.** Open `" + ($rep.name // "") + "` below to read it.")
         elif $repFailed then ("5. **The " + $an + " FAILED.** `" + ($rep.name // "") + "` carries the error instead of a root cause; its page shows it verbatim. This is the hop that fails silently — the alert above still reads as healthy.")
         elif ($rep.state // "") == "Analyzing" then ("5. **The " + $an + " is still running.**")
         else ("5. **The " + $an + " produced nothing.** It wrote neither a root cause nor an error, which is itself the finding.") end),
        (if $rep == null then empty
         elif ($open | length) == 0 then ("6. **No incident is open.** The latest, `" + ($rep.name // "") + "`, is **" + ($rep.state // "Resolved") + "**.")
         elif ($open | length) == 1 then ("6. **Incident** `" + ($open[0].name // "") + "` is **" + ($open[0].state // "Analyzing") + "**.")
         else ("6. **" + ($open | length | tostring) + " incidents are open at once**, each a different problem. The list below has them all.") end)
      ] | join("\n")),
    # The Incidents card: every open incident, then the five latest ended ones, newest first within each.
    incidents: ($open + $ended[0:5] | map({ name, namespace, title, state, when, route })),
    incidentsTitle: ("Incidents · " + ($open | length | tostring) + " open"
      + (if ($ended | length) > 0 then (" · " + ($ended | length | tostring) + " ended" + (if ($ended | length) > 5 then ", the latest 5 shown" else "" end)) else "" end)),
    sections: {
      incident: ($rep != null),
      # Not exception-only: its job is to say which hops SUCCEEDED as well as which stopped,
      # and "all six fine" is the answer someone checking a silent pipeline came for.
      pipeline: ((.alert.metadata.name // "") != ""),
      console: (($console != "") and (($haid != "") or ($hdid != "")))
    },
    # Static GVR for the plain Alert CRD — the DELETE target for button.alert-detail-delete
    # (mirrors composition-detail's .gvr feeding composition-detail-delete). name/namespace come
    # from the fetched CR (falls back to the route params when the read degraded). resource/
    # apiVersion are constant: an Alert is always alerts.observability.krateo.io/v1alpha1.
    gvr: {
      apiVersion: "observability.krateo.io/v1alpha1",
      resource: "alerts",
      name: (.alert.metadata.name // $n),
      namespace: (.alert.metadata.namespace // $ns)
    },
    # The raw Alert CR as a JSON string for the Manifest YamlViewer (managedFields +
    # last-applied stripped; YamlViewer converts JSON → YAML). Empty when the read degraded so
    # the viewer shows its honest empty state, not "{}". Same shape as resource-detail.
    manifestJson: ((.alert // {}) | if (.metadata.name // "") != "" then ((del(.metadata.managedFields, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"])) | tojson) else "" end)
  }

restactions.name: alert-editdef
restactions.filter:
"v1alpha1" as $ver
| (.name // "") as $n
| (.namespace // "default") as $ns
# Collected into an array and indexed, so a CRD that could not be read (or that serves no
# v1alpha1) is null here. A bare `( … ) as $spec` yielded NOTHING then, and a filter with no
# value fails the whole resolve.
| ([ .crd.spec.versions[]? | select(.name == $ver) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec ][0]) as $spec
| (.alert.spec // {}) as $curSpec
| {
    # The CRD spec schema verbatim — no reserved identity fields (name/namespace are fixed on
    # edit). No schema → a form with no fields that says why (the blueprint-formdef pattern).
    schemaSpec: ($spec // { type: "object",
                            title: "The Alert schema could not be read",
                            description: ("The alerts.observability.krateo.io definition did not answer, so there is no form to edit this Alert with. Reload the page; if it persists, the CRD is missing or your account cannot read it."
                                          + (if (.crdError // null) == null then "" else " (" + (.crdError | if type == "array" then .[0] else . end | if type == "object" then (.message // tostring) else tostring end) + ")" end)) }),
    propertiesToHide: [],
    # Pre-fill the form with the Alert's CURRENT spec.
    values: $curSpec,
    gvr: {
      apiVersion: "observability.krateo.io/v1alpha1",
      resource: "alerts",
      name: (.alert.metadata.name // $n),
      namespace: (.alert.metadata.namespace // $ns)
    }
  }

restactions.name: alert-formdef

stages.name: namespaces
stages.filter: [.namespaces.items[] | .metadata.name]

restactions.filter:
"v1alpha1" as $ver
| (.namespaces // []) as $nsAll
| (if ($nsAll | length) > 0 then $nsAll else ["default"] end) as $nsOpts
| (if ($nsOpts | index("default")) then "default" else $nsOpts[0] end) as $nsDefault
| (.crd.spec.versions[]? | select(.name == $ver) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec) as $spec
# Per-user client draft key (localStorage), seeded into initialValues as __owner but never
# rendered/validated — same mechanism as blueprint-create. .username is the snowplow-injected
# JWT principal (identityContext: [username] on the form); absent → "anon".
| (((.username // "anon") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-")) + "__alert-create") as $draftKey
| {
    schemaSpec: (($spec // { type: "object", properties: {} })
      | .properties = ({
          __alert_name__:      { type: "string", title: "Name", description: "Name for the new Alert (metadata.name)." },
          __alert_namespace__: { type: "string", title: "Namespace", description: "Namespace to create the Alert in.", enum: $nsOpts, default: $nsDefault }
        } + (.properties // {}))
      | .required = (["__alert_name__", "__alert_namespace__"] + (.required // []))),
    propertiesToHide: [],
    initialValues: { __owner: $draftKey },
    apiVersion: "observability.krateo.io/v1alpha1",
    kind: "Alert",
    resource: "alerts",
    namespace: $nsDefault
  }

restactions.name: audit-log
restactions.filter:
# Normalise Python isoformat (drop `.ffffff`, fold +00:00 → Z) before parsing; render a compact
# relative age. Unparseable → the raw first-10 (a date).
def rel: (if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("(\\+00:?00)$"; "Z")) else . end) as $norm
  | ($norm | fromdateiso8601? // null) as $t
  | if $t == null then (. // "" | tostring | .[0:10]) else (now - $t) as $dt | (if $dt < 60 then "just now" elif $dt < 3600 then ((($dt/60)|floor|tostring) + "m ago") elif $dt < 86400 then ((($dt/3600)|floor|tostring) + "h ago") elif $dt < 5184000 then ((($dt/86400)|floor|tostring) + "d ago") else .[0:10] end) end;
((.audits.items) // []) as $ars
| ([ $ars[]
     | (.spec // {}) as $sp
     | ($sp.action // {}) as $act
     | {
         # actor — human, or the agent identity when actor=agent (falls back to the enum value).
         actor: (if ($sp.actor // "") == "agent" then ("agent" + (if ($sp.agent.id // "") != "" then (" · " + $sp.agent.id) else "" end)) else ($sp.actor // "—") end),
         verb: (($act.verb // "") | ascii_upcase),
         # resource = "<group>/<resource>/<name>" (gvr + target name), namespace appended when set.
         resource: (((if ($act.group // "") != "" then ($act.group + "/") else "" end) + ($act.resource // "") + "/" + ($act.name // ""))
           + (if ($act.namespace // "") != "" then (" · " + $act.namespace) else "" end)),
         # result — OK/FAILED with the HTTP status; honest "—" when the producer left it unset.
         result: (if ($sp.outcome | type) == "object" then
                    ((if ($sp.outcome.ok // false) then "OK" else "FAILED" end)
                     + (if ($sp.outcome.status // 0) != 0 then (" " + ($sp.outcome.status | tostring)) else "" end))
                  else "—" end),
         resultColor: (if ($sp.outcome.ok // false) then "#389e0d" else (if ($sp.outcome | type) == "object" then "#cf1322" else "#8c8c8c" end) end),
         # timestamp — dispatch time (resolvedAt) preferred, else ask time (requestedAt), else the
         # record's own creationTimestamp; rendered as a compact relative age.
         timestamp: ((($sp.resolvedAt // "") | if . != "" then . else ($sp.requestedAt // "") end
                      | if . != "" then . else (.metadata.creationTimestamp // "") end) | rel),
         # raw sortable key (unnormalised) — newest first.
         ts: (($sp.resolvedAt // $sp.requestedAt // .metadata.creationTimestamp // ""))
       }
   ] | sort_by(.ts) | reverse) as $rows
| { rows: $rows, count: ($rows | length) }

stages.name: prs

[ (.prs.items // [])[]

      state: ((.status.state) // "pending"),
      merged: ((.status.merged) == true),
      # Whether the provider reports `merged` at all — distinct from reporting false. `// false`
      # folds "absent" into "not merged", and those two need opposite rows (see the header).
      mergedKnown: (((.status.merged) | type) == "boolean"),
      # When it merged (portal.builderPrMergedAt): "" unless merged is true.
      mergedAt: (if ((.status.merged) == true) and (((.status.merged_at) | type) == "string") then .status.merged_at else "" end),
      url: ((.status.html_url) // ""),

[ (.publishes.items // [])[]

      branch: (((.status.targetBranch) // (.spec.toRepo.branch)) // ""),
      synced: ([ (.status.conditions // [])[] | select((.type // "") == "Synced") ] | first // {} | (.status // "")),
      # The final filter has always branched on syncReason == "ReconcileError" — and this step
      # never selected it, so `$failed` was unconditionally false and a publish that died hours
      # ago rendered as the orange present participle forever. That is the exact defect the
      # comments further down this file complain about; it was in the step, not the ladder.
      syncReason: ([ (.status.conditions // [])[] | select((.type // "") == "Synced") ] | first // {} | (.reason // "")),
      syncMsg: ([ (.status.conditions // [])[] | select((.type // "") == "Synced") ] | first // {} | (.message // "")),

stages.name: catalog

restactions.filter:
# ending($pr): "merged" | "closed?" | "closed" | "" — see portal.builderPrEnding (_builder.tpl),
# shared with restaction.builder-prs. Legacy and claim rows both use it, so both paths judge a
# merge on the same evidence.
def ending($pr):
  if $pr == null then ""
  elif (($pr.merged) // false) == true then "merged"
  elif ((($pr.state) // "") != "closed") then ""
  elif ((($pr.mergedKnown) // false) | not) then "closed?"
  else "closed" end;
# The Install destination exists only for a row with no CompositionDefinition — once one
# exists the row goes to the blueprint, and a second POST of the same name would 409. Only
# when the CompositionDefinitions could be READ: a failed `cds` step (cdsError) is not
# evidence that there is none. And only for a publish that carries its registration file
# ($hasReg): that file is the whole pre-fill, and without it the form opens on whatever
# helm-index chart shares the name.
((.cdsError // null) == null) as $cdsRead
| def registerable($cd; $end; $hasReg): $cdsRead and $hasReg and $cd == null and ($end == "merged" or $end == "closed?");
(.cds // []) as $cds
| (.prs // []) as $prs
| ((.catalog // []) | map({key: ., value: true}) | from_entries) as $inCatalog
| ([ $prs[]
     | select(((.publish) // "") == "" and ((.repo) // "") == "krateo-blueprints")
     | . as $pr
     | ( [ $cds[] | select(.name == $pr.chart) ] | first ) as $cd
     | ($inCatalog[$pr.chart] // false) as $published
     | ending($pr) as $end
     | { chart: $pr.chart,
         title: $pr.title,
         pr: ("#" + ($pr.number | tostring)),
         url: $pr.url,
         version: (if $cd != null then ("v" + ($cd.version // "?")) else "—" end),
         status: (if ($cd != null and $cd.ready == "True") then "Registered"
                  elif ($cd != null) then "Reconciling"
                  elif $end == "merged" then "Merged"
                  elif ($end == "closed" or $end == "closed?") then "Closed"
                  else "In review" end),
         # Merged is green, the chip the change-request list (restaction.builder-prs) gives the
         # same merged PR: one state, one colour, on both builder pages — and blue there is
         # Open. Registered is still told apart by its label and its empty Next step; a
         # closed change is gray, as on that list.
         statusColor: (if ($cd != null and $cd.ready == "True") then "green"
                       elif ($cd == null and $end == "merged") then "green"
                       elif ($cd == null and ($end == "closed" or $end == "closed?")) then "gray"
                       else "orange" end),
         # What the row click does next, when that is a person's step. Empty otherwise: a
         # row with nothing to do says nothing (exception-only).
         # Legacy rows carry no krateo.io/publish label, so no registration file can be found
         # for them: they are never offered Install ($hasReg false).
         next: (if registerable($cd; $end; false) then (if $end == "merged" then "Install" else "Install if merged" end) else "" end),
         # Marketplace availability — is the chart published to the helm index yet? A chip is
         # rendered ONLY when it is (green "Available"); an unpublished chart shows no chip
         # (exception-only: the calm default is "not yet in the marketplace", no noise).
         marketLabel: (if $published then "Available" else "" end),
         marketColor: (if $published then "green" else "" end),
         ns: "default",
         # Per-row destination, resolved server-side (the Table takes it whole, verbatim).
         # Registered → the blueprint's own page; merged (or closed with no merge signal),
         # unregistered and carrying a registration file → the install form; otherwise the
         # change request; otherwise nothing, and Table.tsx leaves the row inert.
         rowHref: (if $cd != null then ("/blueprints/default/" + $pr.chart)
                   elif registerable($cd; $end; false) then ("/marketplace/" + $pr.chart + "/install")
                   else (($pr.url) // "") end),
         # The merge date, only beside the ending that says merged — never on a "Closed" row.
         mergedAt: (if $end == "merged" then (($pr.mergedAt) // "") else "" end),
         age: $pr.created } ]) as $prRows
| ([ (.publishes // []) | group_by(.publish)[]
     | select((.[0].publish // "") != "")
     | .[0] as $p0
     | ($p0.publish | sub("^publish-"; "")) as $chart
     | ( [ $cds[] | select(.name == $chart) ] | first ) as $cd
     | ($inCatalog[$chart] // false) as $published
     | (all(.[]; .synced == "True")) as $pushed
     | (any(.[]; .syncReason == "ReconcileError")) as $failed
     # The publish carries its root registration file (portal.builderIsRegistrationFile).
     | (any(.[]; .reg == true)) as $hasReg
     | ( [ $prs[] | select(((.publish) // "") == ($p0.publish // "")) ] | first ) as $pr
     | ending($pr) as $end
     | { chart: $chart,
         title: (($pr.title) // ""),
         # builder-publish 1.8.21 opens the change request itself and its CR carries
         # status.html_url, so a claim row finally has somewhere to link. The branch stays the
         # fallback: pullRequest.create can be off, and the chart's CRD guard renders no
         # PullRequest at all on an install below github-provider-kog 0.3.0.
         pr: (if (($pr.number) // 0) > 0 then ("#" + ($pr.number | tostring)) else ($p0.branch // "") end),
         url: (($pr.url) // ""),
         version: (if $cd != null then ("v" + ($cd.version // "?")) else "—" end),
         status: (if ($cd != null and $cd.ready == "True") then "Registered"
                  elif ($cd != null) then "Reconciling"
                  # A change request that has ENDED outranks "In review" — it was the next rung,
                  # and used to swallow closed PRs whole, so a merged blueprint sat "In review"
                  # forever with no way on to its install.
                  elif $end == "merged" then "Merged"
                  elif ($end == "closed" or $end == "closed?") then "Closed"
                  # "In review" USED TO claim a review that provably could not exist: until
                  # builder-publish 1.8.21 the claim path opened no PullRequest at all, the prs step
                  # 404'd under continueOnError, and every row was a claim row wearing a status no
                  # one could act on. A review is real now when its CR exists — and only then.
                  # Without one a pushed branch is still "Pushed", and a failed publish still says
                  # so rather than wearing a present participle.
                  elif ($pr != null and (($pr.number) // 0) > 0) then "In review"
                  elif $pushed then "Pushed"
                  elif $failed then "Publish failed" else "Publishing" end),
         statusColor: (if ($cd != null and $cd.ready == "True") then "green"
                       elif ($cd == null and $end == "merged") then "green"
                       elif ($cd == null and ($end == "closed" or $end == "closed?")) then "gray"
                       else "orange" end),
         next: (if registerable($cd; $end; $hasReg) then (if $end == "merged" then "Install" else "Install if merged" end) else "" end),
         marketLabel: (if $published then "Available" else "" end),
         marketColor: (if $published then "green" else "" end),
         ns: "default",
         rowHref: (if $cd != null then ("/blueprints/default/" + $chart)
                   elif registerable($cd; $end; $hasReg) then ("/marketplace/" + $chart + "/install")
                   else (($pr.url) // "") end),
         mergedAt: (if $end == "merged" then (($pr.mergedAt) // "") else "" end),
         age: ($p0.created // "") } ]) as $claimRows
| (($prRows + $claimRows) | sort_by(.age // "") | reverse) as $rows
| { rows: $rows,
    counts: { total: ($rows | length),
              registered: ([ $rows[] | select(.status == "Registered") ] | length),
              published: ([ $rows[] | select(.marketLabel == "Available") ] | length) } }

restactions.name: blueprint-detail

stages.name: catalog

restactions.filter:
(.name // "") as $n
| (.namespace // "") as $ns
| ((.compdef // {}) | del(.metadata.managedFields, .metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration"])) as $d
| ($d.spec.chart // {}) as $chart
| ($chart.repo // "") as $bp
| ($chart.version // "") as $cur
| ([ (.catalog.entries[$bp]? // [])[] | .version | select(. != null and . != "") ]) as $idxVers
| (($idxVers + [$cur]) | map(select(. != "")) | unique) as $avail
| (if ($idxVers | length) > 0 then ($idxVers | sort | last) else $cur end) as $latest
| ([ $d.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Ready") ][0].status // "Unknown") as $ready
| ([ $d.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Synced") ][0].status // "Unknown") as $synced
| ([ (.comps.items // [])[]
     | { name: (.metadata.name // ""),
         namespace: (.metadata.namespace // ""),
         ready: ([ .status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Ready") ][0].status // "Unknown"),
         synced: ([ .status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Synced") ][0].status // "Unknown"),
         created: (.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
         navHref: ("/compositions/" + (.metadata.namespace // "") + "/" + (.metadata.name // "")),
         readyLabel: ([ .status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Ready") ][0].status // "Unknown" | if . == "True" then "Ready" elif . == "False" then "Failed" else "Pending" end),
         readyColor: ([ .status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Ready") ][0].status // "Unknown" | if . == "True" then "Healthy" elif . == "False" then "Down" else "Pending" end) }
   ] | sort_by(.created) | reverse) as $comps
| {
    detail: $d,
    compositions: $comps,
    compositionsCount: ($comps | length),
    name: ($d.metadata.name // $n),
    namespace: ($d.metadata.namespace // $ns),
    # IA followup F3: forward cross-link to the marketplace catalog entry. $bp is the
    # helm-repo chart name (== the catalog key == the /marketplace/{name} route key),
    # gated on catalog membership so an OCI/platform CD (empty repo) never builds a broken
    # /marketplace/oci://... route — it falls back to the /marketplace index instead.
    marketplaceHref: (if ((((.catalog.entries[$bp]? // []) | length) > 0) and ($bp != "")) then ("/marketplace/" + $bp) else "/marketplace" end),
    inCatalog: ((((.catalog.entries[$bp]? // []) | length) > 0) and ($bp != "")),
    chart: ($chart.repo // ($chart.url // "")),
    chartUrl: ($chart.url // ""),
    currentVersion: $cur,
    availableVersions: $avail,
    latestVersion: $latest,
    updateAvailable: ($latest != $cur and $latest != ""),
    ready: $ready,
    synced: $synced,
    created: ($d.metadata.creationTimestamp // ""),
    versionSchema: {
      type: "object",
      required: ["version"],
      properties: {
        version: { type: "string", title: "Chart version", description: "Select a version to update the blueprint to", enum: $avail }
      }
    },
    versionInitial: { version: $cur },
    gvr: {
      apiVersion: "core.krateo.io/v1alpha1",
      resource: "compositiondefinitions",
      name: ($d.metadata.name // $n),
      namespace: ($d.metadata.namespace // $ns)
    }
  }

restactions.name: blueprint-formdef

stages.name: jsonschema
stages.iterator: [ .compdef | objects | { namespace: (.metadata.namespace // "default"), resource: (.status.resource // ""), version: (((.status.apiVersion // "") | split("/"))[1] // "") } | select(.resource != "" and .version != "") ]

stages.name: crd
stages.iterator: [ .compdef | objects | { resource: (.status.resource // ""), group: (((.status.apiVersion // "") | split("/"))[0] // "") } | select(.resource != "" and .group != "") ]

stages.name: namespaces
stages.filter: [.namespaces.items[] | .metadata.name]

restactions.filter:
# NOT READY — the CompositionDefinition has no generated kind yet (core-provider has not
# reconciled it: the first seconds after an Install), its CRD is not served yet, or this runs with
# no blueprint named (a background prewarm). Every path above is null-safe for it, and the form
# says so instead of failing to resolve: `split` on a null apiVersion used to fail the whole
# widget. The Form widget renders a schema with no fields as its title and description.
(((.username // "anon") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))
    + "__" + ((.namespace // "") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))
    + "__" + ((.name // "") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))) as $ownerKey
| ((.compdef.status.apiVersion // "") | tostring) as $cdApiVersion
| if ($cdApiVersion | contains("/") | not) or ((.compdef.status.resource // "") == "") or ((.crd.spec // null) == null) then
    ([ (.compdef.status.conditions // [])[]? | select(.type == "Ready" and .status == "False") | (.message // "") | select(. != "") ][0]) as $why
    | { stringSchema: "",
        schemaSpec: { type: "object",
                      title: "This blueprint is still being registered",
                      description: ("Its kind has not been generated yet, so there is no form to fill in. This usually takes under a minute — reload the page."
                                    + (if $why == null then "" else " core-provider reports: " + $why end)) },
        propertiesToHide: [],
        initialValues: { __owner: $ownerKey },
        apiVersion: "", kind: "", resource: "" }
  else
($cdApiVersion | split("/")[1]) as $ver
| ((.namespace // "") | if . == "" then "default" else . end) as $blueprintNs
# #66 (tenant self-service): the composition RECORD namespace (metadata.namespace) must be one
# the USER can `create` this composition in — NOT blindly the blueprint's namespace. A tenant's
# blueprints live in a read-only krateo-blueprints ns where the tenant has NO create RBAC, so
# pinning to $blueprintNs made the create POST 403. `.namespaces` is the api-step's
# userAccessFilter output (namespaces where the user CAN create this resource — all existent,
# RBAC-verified). Offer those as the picker; default to $blueprintNs when it's allowed (platform
# admin case → unchanged), else the first allowed ns (tenant case → their own ns). Empty (no
# create RBAC anywhere) → fall back to [$blueprintNs] so the form still renders one option. This
# does NOT reintroduce the old synthetic-`namespace` bug: __composition_namespace__ is an
# UNDERSCORE-FENCED identity key (never collides with a blueprint's own spec `namespace`), and
# every option is a real, create-permitted namespace (no nonexistent-ns 404).
| (.namespaces // []) as $nsAll
| (if ($nsAll | length) > 0 then $nsAll else [$blueprintNs] end) as $nsOpts
| (if ($nsOpts | index($blueprintNs)) then $blueprintNs else $nsOpts[0] end) as $nsDefault
| (.crd.spec.versions[]? | select(.name == $ver) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec) as $spec
# Fields the blueprint marks hidden (title contains "(should be hidden)") are
# omitted from the generated form — propertiesToHide derived from the schema, not hardcoded.
| ([ ($spec.properties // {}) | to_entries[] | select((.value.title // "") | test("should be hidden"; "i")) | .key ]) as $hidden
# Draft key (CLIENT-SIDE resume): per-user (extras.username) + per-blueprint
# (extras.namespace/.name), sanitized to the localStorage-key charset. __owner is the key
# itself — it rides in the form store (initialValues) so the Form knows which localStorage
# entry to read/write, WITHOUT recomputing identity client-side. The draft VALUES live ONLY
# in the browser (localStorage) — never on the backend — so nothing is read for them here.
| (((.username // "anon") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))
    + "__" + ((.namespace // "") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))
    + "__" + ((.name // "") | gsub("[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]"; "-"))) as $draftKey
# stringSchema (authoring order): the blueprint's raw values.schema.json (from the jsonschema
# CM) with __composition_name__/__composition_namespace__ identity STRING-spliced in as the
# first properties and a top-level required injected. Kept as a STRING — never parsed/re-emitted
# — so JSON key order survives to the client (which JSON.parses it). null when the CM is absent
# or has no "properties": — the Form then falls back to schemaSpec. __composition_namespace__ is
# spliced with enum:$nsOpts / default:$nsDefault (the userAccessFilter create-permitted set — see
# the #66 B.2 note above), IDENTICAL to the schemaSpec branch: a picker over namespaces the user
# can create in, defaulting to $blueprintNs when allowed (admin) else the first allowed ns
# (tenant → own ns). Renders single-option/pre-filled only when exactly one ns is permitted.
| ((.jsonschema.data["values.schema.json"]) // null) as $raw
# "" (never null) when there is no raw schema: the Form CRD types stringSchema a string and snowplow
# refuses a resolved widget it does not admit; the Form reads "" as absent and uses schemaSpec.
| (if $raw == null then ""
   else ("\"properties\": ") as $n
     | ($raw | index($n)) as $pi
     | (if $pi == null then ""
        else ($raw[0:($pi + ($n | length))]) as $pfx
          | ($raw[($pi + ($n | length)):]) as $rst
          | ({ __composition_name__:      { type: "string", title: "Name",      description: "Name for the new composition instance" },
               __composition_namespace__: { type: "string", title: "Composition namespace", description: "Where the composition record is created (must be one you can create in) — distinct from any namespace the blueprint itself provisions", enum: $nsOpts, default: $nsDefault } } | tojson) as $id
          | ($pfx + $id[:-1] + "," + $rst[1:]) as $spliced
          # The two identity keys MUST be `required` so they render UP-FRONT, not under the
          # "Advanced" collapse (SchemaFields partitions on required). The old code PREPENDED a
          # "required":[...] key, but the blueprint's raw schema carries its OWN top-level
          # "required" later in the string; JSON.parse's duplicate-key-LAST-wins made the raw one
          # win, dropping the identity keys into Advanced. Fix: read the raw required (read-only
          # parse — the required ARRAY's order is irrelevant to rendering; only PROPERTY order must
          # survive, which the splice above preserves) and APPEND the merged required as the LAST
          # key so it wins. Identity keys first, then the blueprint's own required (minus any dup —
          # the blueprint's own `namespace`, if present, stays required as a real spec field).
          | (((try ($raw | fromjson | .required) catch null) // []) - ["__composition_name__","__composition_namespace__"]) as $rawReq
          | (["__composition_name__","__composition_namespace__"] + $rawReq) as $req
          | (($spliced | sub("\\s+$"; "")) | .[:-1]) as $body
          | ($body + ",\"required\":" + ($req | tojson) + "}")
        end)
   end) as $stringSchema
| {
    stringSchema: $stringSchema,
    schemaSpec: ($spec
      | .properties = ({
          __composition_name__:      { type: "string", title: "Name",      description: "Name for the new composition instance" },
          __composition_namespace__: { type: "string", title: "Composition namespace", description: "Where the composition record is created (must be one you can create in) — distinct from any namespace the blueprint itself provisions", enum: $nsOpts, default: $nsDefault }
        } + (.properties // {}))
      | .required = (["__composition_name__", "__composition_namespace__"] + (.required // []))),
    propertiesToHide: $hidden,
    initialValues: { __owner: $draftKey },
    apiVersion: .compdef.status.apiVersion,
    kind: .compdef.status.kind,
    resource: .compdef.status.resource
  }
  end

restactions.filter:
# cdField / indexEntry / builderChart — portal.builderRegistrationDefs (_builder.tpl), shared
# with restaction.blueprint-install-origin so the note and the pre-fill cannot disagree.
def cdField($k):
  [ split("\n")[]
    | select(test("^\\s+" + $k + ":"))
    | sub("^\\s+" + $k + ":\\s*"; "") | sub("\\s+#.*$"; "") | sub("\\s+$"; "")
    | ltrimstr("\"") | rtrimstr("\"") | ltrimstr("'") | rtrimstr("'") ]
  | first // "";
def indexEntry($bp): (((.catalog.entries[$bp]?) // (.operators.entries[$bp]?) // [])[0]);
def builderFile($bp):
  if $bp == "" then ""
  else ([ ((.builderCds // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end)[]
          | select(((.publish) // "") == ("publish-" + $bp)) | ((.cd) // "") ] | first // "") end;
# The publish's status projection, or null: parsed, and only when it has the three parts Install
# applies — a malformed bundle is no projection, so the install is the plain one.
def builderProjection($bp):
  if $bp == "" then null
  else ([ ((.builderProjections // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end)[]
          | select(((.publish) // "") == ("publish-" + $bp)) | ((.projection) // "") ] | first // "") as $t
       | (if $t == "" then null else (try ($t | fromjson) catch null) end)
       | (if type == "object" and ((.restaction | type) == "object") and ((.apiRef | type) == "object")
               and ((.statusDataTemplate | type) == "array") then . else null end) end;
def builderChart($bp):
  ((indexEntry($bp).urls[0]?) // "") as $indexUrl
  | (if $indexUrl != "" then "" else builderFile($bp) end) as $file
  | { url: ($file | cdField("url")),
      version: ($file | cdField("version") | if . == "CHART_VERSION" then "" else . end) };
# What the install form holds, in the person's words: "controller" for a chart the Controller
# Builder published (krateo.io/builder on its registration file) and the form pre-fills, where the
# step is called Register; "blueprint" for everything else, an index chart included.
def installNoun($bp):
  if (builderChart($bp).url // "") == "" then "blueprint"
  else ([ ((.builderCds // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end)[]
          | select(((.publish) // "") == ("publish-" + $bp)) | ((.builder) // "") ] | first // "")
       | if . == "controller" then "controller" else "blueprint" end end;
def withLive:
  (((.catalogLive // {}) | if type == "object" then (.entries // {}) else {} end) | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $live
  | (((.catalog // {}) | if type == "object" then . else {} end)) as $cat
  | (($cat.entries // {}) | if type == "object" then . else {} end) as $cur
  | .catalog = ($cat | .entries = ($cur + ($live | with_entries(select(($cur[.key] == null) and ((.value | type) == "array") and ((((.value[0] // {}) | if type == "object" then ((.annotations // {})["krateo.io/source-repo"] // "") else "" end) | tostring) != "")) | .value |= map(select(type == "object") | . + {repoBase: "https://krateo-blueprints.github.io/charts/blueprints"}))))) ;
# Drop statusDataTemplate — it's a blueprint-author field (status projection), not something
# the installer sets; remove it from the fetched CRD schema so it doesn't render in the form.
(.crd.spec.versions[]? | select(.name == "v1alpha1") | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec | del(.properties.statusDataTemplate)) as $spec0
# Strip nested `required` arrays so the optional objects (apiRef / deploy / chart.credentials)
# don't block submit when left empty. chart.url is pre-filled so it still rides through; only
# the synthetic top-level `name` stays required (set below).
| ($spec0 | .properties = ((.properties // {}) | walk(if (type == "object" and has("required")) then del(.required) else . end))) as $spec
| (.name // "") as $bp
| .namespaces as $namespaces
| ((.targets // []) | map(select(. != null and . != ""))) as $targetNames
# Resolve the selected item across BOTH helm indexes (blueprints first, then operators).
# A helm-repo entry carries urls[0] = the full .tgz URL and version. The core-provider
# ChartInfo convention (verified in krateo-platformops/core-provider types.go + composition.go:
# Reconcile is called with URL=chart.url, ChartName=chart.repo, ChartVersion=chart.version)
# for a helm-repo-INDEX install is: chart.url = the repo BASE URL (tgz filename stripped),
# chart.repo = the chart NAME, chart.version = the version. That is exactly what the
# marketplace catalog's installed-join keys on (restaction.blueprints-catalog). So for an
# operator like ec2-chart this yields url=https://krateo-blueprints.github.io/charts/operators,
# repo=ec2-chart, version=1.15.2 — a well-formed CD (chart.url is non-empty, so it survives
# the form's empty-prune and satisfies the CRD's required:[url]).
#
# OCI entries differ: for an oci:// urls[0] the core-provider convention (installer definitions.yaml:
# OCI branch) is chart.url = the FULL oci ref (oci://<base>/<name>, NOT filename-stripped) and NO
# chart.repo (appending the name to url would double it). So branch on the url scheme below: oci://
# keeps the raw url + omits repo; a helm-repo url strips the filename + carries repo=name.
#
# A chart only the LIVE blueprints index carries (withLive, _catalog.tpl) comes last: after both
# indexes and after a builder publish of the name (builderChart, which reads the two indexes
# only, wins over it below). Its tarball sits in a GitHub release, not beside index.yaml, so its
# repo URL is the channel's base it carries as repoBase, not the stripped tarball URL.
| (indexEntry($bp) // (withLive | indexEntry($bp))) as $entry
| ($entry.version // "") as $ver
| ($entry.urls[0]? // "") as $rawUrl
| ($entry.repoBase // ($rawUrl | sub("/[^/]+$"; ""))) as $repoUrl
# The builder publish, when this chart came from one: builder-publish names the claim
# "publish-<chart>" and labels every file it commits with that claim, so the route's `name`
# selects the claim's own registration file. Only for a name no helm index carries: this route
# is also the official marketplace card, and an index name keeps its index chart — a builder
# claim that shares the name must not re-point it (builderChart, _builder.tpl). A builder chart
# is published to GHCR, never to an index, so for every other name the builder file is the
# only pre-fill there is. CHART_VERSION (a page set's placeholder) comes back as "".
| builderChart($bp) as $b
| ($b.url // "") as $bUrl
| ($b.version // "") as $bVer
# A controller is registered, not installed: the copy follows what the form holds.
| installNoun($bp) as $noun
# HOW THE DEFINITION UPGRADES, SET EXPLICITLY. core-provider's upgradePolicy defaults to
# Automatic: every live instance is migrated onto a new chart version the moment the definition
# serves it, with no approval. A controller's instances are external resources a person
# depends on, so a controller registers Manual (new versions are served beside the old; an
# instance moves when annotated krateo.io/upgrade-to-version). A blueprint or page set keeps
# Automatic — but written out, so the choice is visible in the form and in the object rather
# than inherited from a default that could change.
# A controller's CDC also resyncs every 4h instead of the chart-global 3m: its instances change
# rarely, so a full re-list every three minutes is near-idle churn. The cost, said in the help:
# drift in what it renders (a hand-edited RestDefinition) waits for the resync. Each key only when the served CRD has it (an older core-provider does not).
| ($spec.properties.upgradePolicy != null) as $hasPolicy
| (($spec.properties.controller.properties.resyncInterval? // null) != null) as $hasResync
| (if $noun == "controller" then "Manual" else "Automatic" end) as $policy
| ((if $hasPolicy then { upgradePolicy: $policy } else {} end)
   + (if $hasResync and $noun == "controller" then { controller: { resyncInterval: "4h" } } else {} end)) as $specBase
| {
    schemaSpec: ($spec
      | .properties = ({
          name: { type: "string", title: "Name", description: (if $noun == "controller" then "Name for the registered controller (the CompositionDefinition)" else "Name for the installed blueprint (the CompositionDefinition)" end) },
          namespace: { type: "string", title: "Namespace", description: (if $noun == "controller" then "Namespace to register the controller in" else "Namespace to install the blueprint into" end), enum: $namespaces }
        } + (.properties // {}))
      | .required = (["name", "namespace"] + (.required // []))
      | (if (($targetNames | length) > 0) and ((.properties.deploy.properties.targetRef.properties.name? // null) != null)
         then (.properties.deploy.properties.targetRef.properties.name |= (. + { title: "Deploy to cluster", description: "Leave empty to deploy on this (hub) cluster; pick a registered spoke to deploy remotely.", enum: $targetNames }))
         else . end)
      # A builder chart is OCI, and for OCI the version is not optional (the CRD: "needed for
      # oci charts"). The strip above made every chart field optional, which in the sectioned
      # Form also files them under the chart section's collapsed "Advanced" group
      # (SchemaFields partitions on each object's own `required`). So for a builder chart only,
      # url and version are required again: both sit up-front where the person reviews them,
      # and a page set cannot be installed until the person types its tag — instead of
      # POSTing a CompositionDefinition with no version, which the pruning would let through.
      # The empty version also says why it is empty and what to do about it, in the person's
      # terms: a page set's merge releases nothing (the scaffold releases a placeholder
      # version only from a tag), so the step before this one is pushing that tag. Every
      # other install keeps exactly the schema it had.
      | (if $bUrl != "" and ((.properties.chart.properties? // null) != null)
         then (.properties.chart.required = ["url", "version"])
              | (if $bVer == "" and ((.properties.chart.properties.version? // null) != null)
                 then (.properties.chart.properties.version |= (. + { description: "A page set's merge releases nothing. Push a semver tag on main in its repository (git tag 0.1.0 origin/main && git push origin 0.1.0), wait for that release to go green, then type the tag here." }))
                 else . end)
         else . end)
      # Up front, with the reason, beside the fields the person reviews.
      | (if $hasPolicy
         then (.properties.upgradePolicy |= (. + { default: $policy, description:
                (if $noun == "controller"
                 then "Manual: a new version of this controller is served beside the old one, and an existing instance moves to it only when you annotate it krateo.io/upgrade-to-version. Each republish therefore leaves the previous version's controller running until every instance has been moved that way. Automatic would migrate every live instance as soon as the chart version moves, with no approval."
                 else "Automatic: every instance installed from this chart moves to a new chart version as soon as it is registered. Choose Manual to keep instances on their version until you annotate one krateo.io/upgrade-to-version, or Paused to never migrate them." end) }))
              | .required = ((.required // []) + ["upgradePolicy"])
         else . end)
      | (if $hasResync and $noun == "controller"
         then (.properties.controller.properties.resyncInterval |= (. + { description:
                "4h: how often this controller re-reads every instance and the resources it renders, to correct drift. A change to an instance is picked up when it is made, but a manual change to what it renders (a RestDefinition or Configuration edited or deleted by hand) can stay for up to four hours before it is corrected. The default is three minutes." }))
              | .properties.controller.required = ["resyncInterval"]
              | .required = ((.required // []) + ["controller"])
         else . end)),
    initialValues: ({
      name: $bp,
      namespace: "default",
      chart: (if $bUrl != "" then { url: $bUrl, version: $bVer }
              elif ($rawUrl | startswith("oci://")) then { url: $rawUrl, version: $ver }
              else { url: $repoUrl, repo: $bp, version: $ver } end)
    } + $specBase),
    # Merged UNDER the form's spec on submit (form.blueprint-install), so the policy and the
    # resync are written even when the person never opens the section that shows them.
    specBase: $specBase,
    noun: $noun,
    apiVersion: "core.krateo.io/v1alpha1",
    kind: "CompositionDefinition",
    resource: "compositiondefinitions",
    # A builder chart's status projection (S12): the <chart>-status RESTAction and the apiRef and
    # rows its CompositionDefinition carries. Null for every other install — the form then keeps
    # its one plain write.
    projection: (if $bUrl != "" then builderProjection($bp) else null end)
  }
